review.title: A Tauri v2 shell that owns the sidecar's lifetime
review.acceptance: A Tauri v2 application starts, spawns the PW-0101 sidecar, reads its bound port from stdout, points the webview at it, and cannot leave the sidecar running. REQUIRED: the Tauri version is pinned exactly, on the rule this repository already applies to Shaka and Playwright -- a caret range means the shell a gate was recorded against can change under a lockfile refresh. REQUIRED: the sidecar is packaged as node.exe plus the standalone tree under bundle.resources and spawned as a child process; pkg, Node SEA and Bun --compile are documented as unable to swallow a Next standalone server and must not be attempted as a shortcut. REQUIRED: a Win32 Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, because Tauri provides no supervision and an orphaned node.exe holding a loopback port is the failure a user sees as 'it will not start the second time'. REQUIRED: supervision -- health check, restart with a bounded attempt budget, and an honest surfaced failure when the budget is spent, never a blank window. REQUIRED: the shell passes the bearer token to the sidecar through the environment and never on a command line, where it would be readable from the process list. STATED LIMITATION TO CARRY IN THE GATE EVIDENCE: no Windows binary can be produced or run from the cloud session, so this task's build gate is cargo check plus a windows-latest CI job, and 'it launches' is real-device evidence owed to PW-0601.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on a3d70f5. cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, FULL TREE, exit 0. cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings for BOTH targets, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, zero errors -- added because the new CI job runs it and a gate that does not run what CI runs is a gate that discovers its findings on the runner. It found two real ones in existing code and both were fixed rather than allowed: a very complex boxed-closure type in a test, and a loop that is a while-let. Monorepo unchanged: npm run typecheck 21/21, npm run lint 11/11 zero problems, npm run repo:validate passed. The new workflow parses as YAML with one job, windows-shell, on windows-latest, seven steps. ONE PACKAGING FACT FOUND AND FIXED: apps/desktop/dist/index.html was silently ignored by the ROOT .gitignore's dist/ rule. Everywhere else in this repository dist/ is build output; here it is a single hand-written failure page named by tauri.conf.json as frontendDist, with no build step that could regenerate it, so an ignored copy means a packaged shell with no page to show when it has something to say. Un-ignored by exception in apps/desktop/.gitignore with the reason recorded there.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on a3d70f5. cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -> 42 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, up from 25. Monorepo suite unchanged at 20/20 with apps/web at 1109; this task adds no TypeScript. THE SEVENTEEN NEW TESTS ARE ABOUT THE ASSEMBLY, which is what the round-87 verdict said was missing, and they are possible because the assembly is a SEQUENCE behind a trait rather than a function full of syscalls. THE CENTRAL ORDERING ASSERTION: create_job before spawn, spawn before assign, assign before the handshake, handshake before show_window -- each checked by position in a recorded call list. A job created after the spawn has nothing to assign; a window shown before a handshake is a window pointed at a port nothing is listening on. THE TOKEN, at the point where a process is actually created: absent from every spawn argument, present in the environment under LIBERTY_SIDECAR_TOKEN. sidecar.rs already asserts this of launch_arguments; this re-asserts it where somebody would one day add an argument. A TOKEN THAT CANNOT BE MINTED STOPS THE LAUNCH: nothing is spawned and a failure is surfaced, because every fallback source is predictable to the local processes the token excludes. A JOB THAT CANNOT BE CREATED REFUSES TO START rather than running unsupervised, and the surfaced text is asserted to explain that choice -- a user not told why nothing opened will think it crashed. A CHILD THAT CANNOT BE ASSIGNED IS KILLED, asserted by position: the kill follows the failed assign and no window is shown. An unassigned running child is the orphan itself. THE ORIGIN COMES FROM WHAT THE CHILD REPORTED: an IPv6 handshake produces http://[::1]:50000, bracketed, because the unbracketed form is not a URL and the shell would silently fail to navigate. A REJECTED HANDSHAKE IS NOT RETRIED -- exactly one spawn -- because a broken contract will not fix itself on the fourth attempt and retrying delays the message that says what happened. A TIMEOUT IS RETRIED WITHIN THE BUDGET AND THEN SURFACED, bounded between two and six spawns. A HEALTHY RUN THAT ENDS IS RESTARTED AND A FLAPPING ONE IS NOT, which exercises the supervision policy THROUGH the assembly rather than only in isolation, so the loop must actually consult it. A MISSING INSTALLATION IS NOT RETRIED and never reaches a job. AND NO FAILURE PATH PANICS: eight distinct failures are each run and each asserted to surface something, because a shell that panics is a window that closes itself. THE TOKEN MODULE ADDS FIVE: the minted token satisfies TOKEN_MIN_CHARS as lower-case hex asserted against the constant rather than the literal; 64 mints produce 64 distinct tokens, because per-launch is the whole property; 256 tokens are checked for prefix distinctness and hex-digit distribution, which is not a statistical test and is not claimed as one -- it catches a source that is a counter, a timestamp or a padded constant; hex encoding is checked directly; and a source scan asserts the module reaches for no SystemTime, Instant, process::id, rand:: or hostname. THAT LAST TEST FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN by matching its own forbidden-word list, which is a guard matching prose about the thing rather than the thing -- the fifth instance in this repository and written minutes after PL-AI-0013 was approved for that class. It is scoped to the code above the test module and the comment records the miss. ONE HARNESS DEFECT WORTH RECORDING: the fake's first draft repeated its last run duration forever, and with a healthy duration that is an infinite loop -- the suite was SIGKILLed. That is not a defect in run_shell: a sidecar that runs for an hour and exits SHOULD be restarted. It is a fake that could promise an endless supply of healthy runs, which no machine does.

build.evidence: RE-RECORDED on a3d70f5. STILL FAIL, and now for exactly one reason: THE WINDOWS JOB HAS NOT RUN, BECAUSE THE BRANCH CANNOT BE PUSHED. The round-87 ruling set the procedure precisely -- implement the corrective, run the local gates, then push so GitHub Actions can execute the new windows-latest job, record the real job result, and keep build FAIL if the Windows job itself fails. Every step was executed except the push. git push origin codex/pl-ai-0001-repair returns HTTP 403 from the git proxy: CrownOwlP/project-liberty is not in this session's authorized repository set. That has been true for every round since 81 and is a commander-level unblock, not something this task can route around. THE WORKFLOW EXISTS AND IS READY: .github/workflows/desktop-shell-ci.yml, windows-latest, Rust pinned to 1.90.0 rather than stable -- because a gate is recorded against what was built and stable can change under the next run with no commit saying so -- cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets with warnings denied, cargo build --locked --release, and the unsigned binary uploaded for later smoke evidence. --locked on every step, because without it Cargo may quietly update the lockfile and CI would verify a graph that is not the committed one, which is precisely the failure ADR-009 records. It carries no signing, no MSI or NSIS packaging, no installer or update evidence and no release artifact responsibility; those remain PW-0501's, and the file states what it must never grow into. WHAT WAS RUN LOCALLY AND PASSES, recorded under typecheck and unit rather than smuggled in here: the full-tree Windows cross-check, clippy for both targets with warnings denied, and 42 unit tests including seventeen that assert the startup ORDER itself. WHAT IS STILL NOT EVIDENCED BY ANYTHING: that the shell launches, that WebView2 renders, that the Job Object terminates the sidecar, that an installer works. A cross-compile check never links and is not a build; a unit test of an ordering never starts a process. This gate stays FAIL until the windows-latest job has actually run and its result is recorded here -- and if that job fails, it stays FAIL then too.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED at 25af05d0676507488c37bba9143a1e675722e3c3. TRANSCRIBED BY CLAUDE from gpt-architect's round-87 verdict. ACCEPTED: the Tauri dependency correction; tauri 2.12.0 with zero manually pinned transitive dependencies is the correct graph; ADR-009 correctly preserves the failed 2.9.1 episode as history rather than rewriting it away; the Windows cross-target check is valid evidence and the Win32_Security correction it found is real; and the build gate must remain FAIL. THE BLOCKING DEFECT: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs::run() intentionally panics, so the application cannot start. The modules implement pieces of the shell but are not assembled into a shell. Windows is required to VERIFY the assembly, not to WRITE it. REQUIRED CORRECTIVE, eleven items: mint the per-launch sidecar token from a CSPRNG, not timestamps, UUID formatting, PRNGs or predictable process state, preserving the 64-character hex contract; build the Tauri application using the reviewed v2 configuration with the main window hidden until the sidecar is ready; resolve the packaged resource directory through Tauri's supported resource API; build and execute the existing SidecarLaunch plan, spawning the bundled node.exe with server.js as argv and token, host and port passed only through the environment as already designed; capture sidecar stdout and parse the existing handshake contract; create the Windows Job Object and assign the sidecar process to it; on a valid handshake construct the loopback origin from the reported bound port, navigate the WebView to it and show the window; on an invalid handshake, a failed startup or an early child death use the existing failure vocabulary and surface an actionable application failure rather than panicking or exiting silently; wire the existing bounded supervision policy; on normal application exit close or terminate the Job Object so the sidecar cannot survive the desktop process; and keep the security separation intact -- the launch token authenticates the local listener, never becomes account authentication, and is never logged or placed in argv. BUILD-GATE DEADLOCK BROKEN BY RULING: PW-0102 may add ONE narrow workflow, .github/workflows/desktop-shell-ci.yml or a uniquely named equivalent owned only by PW-0102, existing solely to establish this task's shell build evidence -- windows-latest, a pinned Rust toolchain, cargo test, a full-tree cargo check or build for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, preferably producing the unsigned shell artifact needed for smoke evidence, with no release signing and no production installer or release responsibility. PW-0501 remains the owner of the production packaging and release workflow and must not co-own this one; PW-0602 remains the certification consumer. The surface extension must be recorded in the control plane before it is taken.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
